The Cachara, Pseudoplatystoma reticulatum, is a large pimelodid catfish native to the Paraná-Paraguay River basin, where it occupies deep channel habitats and floodplain environments. Reproductive biology studies conducted under controlled conditions at a stable water temperature of 25 °C [T = 25 °C] have provided detailed insight into its ovarian dynamics. The gonadosomatic index (GSI) for reproductively active females reaches a mean value of 20% [GSI = 20%] at a water temperature of 25 °C [T = 25 °C]. This metric was derived from gravid individuals collected during the peak spawning season and subsequently held in laboratory tanks to ensure thermal consistency. The species is an iteroparous spawner, with females producing multiple batches of adhesive, demersal eggs over an extended reproductive period that coincides with the rising waters of the austral spring and summer.

Size-based maturation schedules have been inferred from extensive field sampling across the upper Paraguay River system. The total length at which 50 percent of females have attained puberty is 25 cm [Lp = 25 cm], a value that places the onset of reproductive capability at a relatively modest body size compared to congeneric species such as Pseudoplatystoma corruscans. This length threshold corresponds roughly to the second year of life under typical floodplain growth conditions. The ultimate standard length, representing the asymptotic maximum size approached by older adults in natural populations, has been estimated at 60.5 cm [Li = 60.5 cm]. This asymptotic length is considerably smaller than the historical maxima reported for the species from the lower Paraná, possibly reflecting contemporary size-selective fishing pressure that truncates the age structure and removes the largest individuals before they can be recorded.

Early life history traits are strongly influenced by incubation temperature, with experimental rearing at 25 °C [T = 25 °C] producing a consistent developmental timeline. The duration from fertilization to hatching, defined as the age at birth for the free-swimming yolk-sac larva, is 8 days [ab = 8 days] at this thermal regime at a temperature of 25 °C [T = 25 °C]. Upon emergence, the prolarvae possess a substantial yolk reserve that sustains them through the lecithotrophic phase prior to the onset of exogenous feeding. The wet weight at birth, estimated from the mean egg diameter of related species and confirmed through volumetric displacement, is approximately 0.0028 g [Wwb = approximately 0.0028 g]. This minute mass, typical of siluriform eggs that are small and numerous, underscores a reproductive strategy prioritizing high fecundity over large offspring size, an adaptation to the unpredictable availability of planktonic prey in dynamic river-floodplain systems.

Longitudinal growth data from both mark-recapture studies and otolith-based age assignments indicate that the species adheres to a moderately paced life history for a large-bodied freshwater teleost. At the standard experimental temperature of 25 °C [T = 25 °C], the maximum lifespan recorded under natural conditions is approximately 9 years [am = approximately 9 years], with very few individuals surviving beyond this age in contemporary, exploited populations. This longevity estimate aligns reasonably well with values reported for other pimelodids of similar asymptotic size, though historical accounts suggest that unexploited cohorts may have attained somewhat greater ages prior to the intensification of commercial fishing in the twentieth century. The combination of a moderate lifespan with an early size at puberty allows for multiple reproductive episodes across an individual's lifetime, a classic iteroparous strategy that confers resilience against years of poor recruitment.

Comparative life-history analysis within the Pimelodidae places Pseudoplatystoma reticulatum as an intermediate strategist relative to its congeners. At 25 °C [T = 25 °C], the ultimate standard length of 60.5 cm [Li = 60.5 cm] is notably smaller than that of Pseudoplatystoma fasciatum in the Amazon, yet the total length at puberty of 25 cm [Lp = 25 cm] is reached at a comparable early size, suggesting a conserved threshold for reproductive activation within the genus. The gonadosomatic index was 20% [GSI = 20%] at a temperature of 25 °C [T = 25 °C]. The wet weight at birth of 0.0028 g [Wwb = 0.0028 g] and the brief incubation period of 8 days [ab = 8 days] together reflect a selective environment that favors rapid hatching and larval dispersal into floodplain nursery habitats, where mortality risks are high but growth potential is immense during the brief productive season at a temperature of 25 °C [T = 25 °C].
